holidays.name: Hobbit Day
holidays.description: Second breakfast is encouraged. Fans of Middle-earth celebrate the birthday of Bilbo and Frodo Baggins. Popular ways to mark it include a hobbit-style feast, a barefoot stroll, and a Tolkien movie marathon.
holidays.origin: In J.R.R. Tolkien's stories, Bilbo and Frodo Baggins share a birthday on September 22. Tolkien fans and Tolkien societies have honored the date for decades. Hobbit Day is usually celebrated as part of a week that also includes Tolkien's own birthday.
holidays.funFact: Bilbo's famous 111th birthday party kicks off The Lord of the Rings. Bilbo and Frodo's shared birthday is a plot point in the books, so it is no accident the fandom picked this date.

holidays.name: Elephant Appreciation Day
holidays.description: This day honors the largest land animals on Earth. It celebrates their intelligence, their close family bonds, and their very good memories. It is also a nudge to support the conservation of both African and Asian elephants.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. Wildlife lovers and conservation groups have embraced it as a day to spotlight elephants and the threats they face.
holidays.funFact: Elephant herds are led by an older matriarch. She guides the group to water and food using decades of memory.

holidays.name: Ice Cream Cone Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the crunchy, handheld vessel that keeps your scoop off your plate. Cake cone, waffle cone, or sugar cone, the only rule is to eat it before it melts down your wrist.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It honors the edible cone, which became hugely popular in the early 1900s.
holidays.funFact: Edible cones are often tied to the 1904 World's Fair in St. Louis. Vendors there helped turn them into a national sensation.
